title: Convert Complete BST to Min Heap
statement:
You are given a binary search tree with distinct values that is also a **complete binary tree**: every level is full except possibly the last, and the last level is filled from the left. Convert it into a **min-heap** in `O(n)` time. You must not create or remove nodes: the shape of the tree stays exactly the same, only the values stored in the nodes are rewritten (the set of values is unchanged).

A min-heap needs every node to be smaller than its children, but many rearrangements of the values satisfy that. To make the answer unique, the converted tree must also keep the BST-like ordering between siblings: for every node, **all values in its left subtree are smaller than all values in its right subtree**.

Because the tree is complete, it is given in level order and no `null` appears: the node at index `i` has children at indices `2i + 1` and `2i + 2`. Print the values of the converted tree in level order.

**Follow-up:** before this problem the interviewer asked what a heap is, the types of heap, and for dry runs of heap insertion and of heapify. Be ready to walk through those on a small example.
inputFormat: A single line containing the `n` values of the tree in level order, separated by spaces (the tree is complete, so there are no `null` entries).
outputFormat: Print the `n` values of the converted min-heap in level order, separated by spaces.
constraints: The input is a valid BST and a complete binary tree (so its depth is at most 17)

examples.explanation: The in-order sequence 1 2 3 4 5 6 is handed out in pre-order over the same shape. The root gets 1. Its left subtree (three nodes) gets 2, 3, 4 with 2 at the top, and the right subtree (two nodes) gets 5, 6 with 5 at the top.
The root takes 10. The left subtree takes 20 (root), 30, 40 and the right subtree takes 50 (root), 60, 70.
A single node is already a heap.

hints: An in-order traversal of a BST visits the values in sorted order, so you get the sorted values in O(n) without sorting.

A min-heap with the left-before-right rule is exactly what you get by writing the sorted values back in pre-order (node, then left subtree, then right subtree): the root receives the smallest value, and each subtree receives a consecutive block of values.
Index the tree as an array: the children of i are 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. Do both traversals on indices (iteratively, or recursively since the depth is at most 17).
